statCallout.context: New assemblies must also be tested immediately after installation.

sections.title: Why Utilities Treat Backflow Testing as More Than Paperwork
body: A backflow prevention assembly protects the public drinking-water system from a reversal of flow at a customer connection. SFPUC lists boilers, chemical-feed equipment, dedicated irrigation, interconnected fire sprinklers, taller buildings, and elevated water supplies among the property conditions that can create a potential cross-connection or hazard under its ordinance.

The annual field test is the operating evidence that the required assembly still performs. A tag, old report, invoice, or photo does not establish the result of the current test. If an assembly fails, the compliance workflow normally continues through repair or replacement, a passing retest, and the report or portal submission required by the serving utility.

Utilities therefore have a water-quality reason to enforce the program. The exact enforcement tool is local, but the underlying control is consistent: identify the hazard, use the required protection, test it on schedule, and document the result.

sections.title: Turn the Utility Notice Into a Closed Compliance Record
body: Use the notice as the start of a tracked job rather than treating the field visit as the finish line.
bullets: Confirm the service address, utility account, assembly location, make, model, size, and serial number.
Verify the due date, submission method, and tester credential accepted by the serving utility.
Schedule early enough to absorb locked access, damaged test ports, failed components, parts delays, and a required retest.
Keep the field-test report with repair documentation and the final passing result.
Submit through the utility's required channel and retain confirmation rather than assuming the tester visit automatically closed the notice.
For portfolios and HOAs, track each assembly separately so one passing device does not hide an overdue device at the same property.

sections.title: Your Serving Utility Controls the Customer-Facing Process
body: California's statewide cross-connection framework sits behind local administration. The serving public water system identifies covered premises, communicates testing requirements, recognizes the tester path, receives results, and handles customer enforcement through its own program.

That is why a San Francisco consequence cannot be copied into an Inland Empire notice as though it were the same rule. It is also why owners should not rely on a generic internet deadline. The current utility notice and program instructions are the account-specific sources for what must be submitted and when.

Backflow Test Pros can help identify the assembly, coordinate certified testing, complete repair and retesting when needed, and organize the documentation. The utility remains the authority for the account's deadline, acceptance, and enforcement status.

sections.title: Backflow Non-Compliance FAQ
body: These answers separate the documented utility example from the steps that are useful on any account.

faqItems.question: Will every utility shut off water after one missed test?
faqItems.answer: No universal sequence applies to every utility. SFPUC lists termination, fines, or both as possible consequences, but your serving utility's current notice and program rules control your account.

faqItems.question: Does paying for a test automatically close the notice?
faqItems.answer: Not necessarily. The assembly must be tested, any failure must be corrected and retested, and the result must reach the utility through its accepted submission process.

faqItems.question: What if the notice lists an assembly I cannot find?
faqItems.answer: Do not ignore it or substitute a different device. Confirm the service address and assembly details with the utility, then arrange a site review before the deadline.

faqItems.question: How early should testing be scheduled?
faqItems.answer: Early enough to leave room for access issues, repairs, replacement parts, a passing retest, and report submission. The exact buffer depends on the due date and the utility's process.

faqItems.question: Who decides whether my property is compliant?
faqItems.answer: The serving utility or responsible public authority administers the account requirement. A tester documents assembly performance; the utility controls acceptance and enforcement status.
